new_roles.title: Head of Technical Operations (TechOps)
new_roles.description:
Join Formlabs if you want to bring ground-breaking professional 3D printers to the desktop of every designer, engineer, researcher, and artist in the world.

 As the Head of Technical Operations (TechOps) at Formlabs, you will own the foundation the whole company runs on: our global network, on-premise servers, endpoints, IT service desk, identity and access, and the security program that protects Formlabs and our customers’ data. This is a single, combined leadership role — where you will lead as a player-coach.

 You will lead a global team of 7 spanning network administration, systems administration, help desk, and cybersecurity, and support offices in Somerville, Germany, Budapest, and Shenzhen.

 You will join the Systems team, which enables every Formlabs team with enterprise applications, infrastructure, data, AI, and security. You will report to the CIO.

 This role is based in our Somerville, MA office and is an onsite role. 

 The Job: 

 
 Team Leadership: Lead, coach, and develop a team of 7 across network, systems, help desk, and cybersecurity. Set clear priorities, build strong technical leadership within the team, and grow the team’s automation and scripting skills.

 Network & Connectivity: Own our Cisco Meraki estate across four countries — SD-WAN and site-to-site VPN, firewalls, segmentation, Wi-Fi, ISP circuits, cloud VPN tunnels, remote access, and the specific connectivity and compliance requirements of operating in China.

 Strategy & Roadmap: Define and drive a combined infrastructure and security roadmap that balances reliability, risk, cost, and user experience — and explain it in business terms to the CIO, CFO, and company leadership. 

 Servers & Resilience: Own on-premise compute (Proxmox) and the services that run on it — lifecycle, patching, monitoring, backup and tested restores, and disaster recovery — and make deliberate decisions about what stays on-prem versus moves to cloud or SaaS.

 Security Program: Own Formlabs’ cybersecurity program end to end: policy, risk register, vulnerability and patch management, endpoint protection, email and SaaS security, logging, data loss prevention, and incident detection, response runbooks, and exercises.

 Staffing Model & Services: Provide leadership on how the team is staffed and which services it relies on — deciding what to build in-house versus source from managed service and security partners — and hold those partners accountable to clear scope and SLAs.

 Identity & Access: Own the joiner/mover/leaver process, SSO and MFA, privileged and break-glass access, and admin hygiene across Google Workspace and core SaaS — with the evidence trail auditors expect.

 IT Service Desk & Endpoints: Ensure a fast, friendly, measurable help desk for ~800 employees — ticket SLAs, onboarding/offboarding, laptop lifecycle and MDM, conference room and A/V, and site support — and personally own the hardest escalations.

 Automation & AI: Replace manual, repeatable work with automation and AI-assisted workflows across provisioning, monitoring, ticket triage, and reporting, so the team scales with the company.

 Vendors & Budget: Own the infrastructure and security vendor portfolio and budget — contracts, renewals, licensing, and hardware refresh plans — and make clear build/buy/partner tradeoffs.

 Documentation & Continuity: Maintain current diagrams, inventories, runbooks, and on-call/escalation coverage so no system depends on a single person’s knowledge.

 
 You: 

 
 Experience: 8+ years in IT infrastructure and/or security, including 2+ years leading teams, ideally in a mid-sized (500–2,000 person) company with multiple international sites.

 Network & Systems Depth: Hands-on expertise in enterprise networking (routing, VPN, firewalls, segmentation, Wi-Fi) and server virtualization; you can review a firewall rule set or a backup design yourself.

 Security Leadership: Practical experience building or running a security program at a company without a large dedicated security team — including EDR, identity, vulnerability management, and incident response.

 Service Mindset: You care how employees experience IT, measure service quality, and lead a help desk with the same rigor as a network.

 Vendor Management: Proven ability to design a team’s staffing and sourcing model, and to select, negotiate with, and hold managed service providers accountable.

 Communication: Translate technical risk into clear business decisions for executives, and write clear policies, runbooks, and recommendations.

 Controls & Compliance: Experience with frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27001, or SOC 2, and with IT general controls in an audit-ready environment.

 Bachelor’s degree in a technical field or equivalent experience.

 
 Bonus Points: 

 
 Experience with Cisco Meraki, Proxmox, CrowdStrike, Google Workspace, and Cloudflare.

 Experience operating IT in China (cross-border connectivity, local regulations, remote-site support).

 Familiarity with GCP and AWS security fundamentals (IAM, logging, network controls).

 Scripting/automation skills (Python, PowerShell, Terraform, or similar) and hands-on use of AI tools in IT or security operations.

 Security certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or CCNP Security.

 Experience in a hardware or manufacturing company with R&D labs and lab networks.

 
 Our Benefits & Perks: 

 
 Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs

 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)

 401K matching and access to financial advisors

 Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)

 Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)

 Flexible Out of Office Plan – Take time when you need it

 Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits

 Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats

 Regular sponsored professional development opportunities

 Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community

 And of course… unlimited 3D prints

 
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company.  We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.   

 Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.

 Our Candidate AI Guidelines are available here . Please give them a read.
 Compensation: 
 

 Equity is a big part of the compensation package at Formlabs - every employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. We have a lot of confidence in the products we’re building and the impact we’re making, and you should too.

 Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.

 The annual base pay range for this role is:
 $150,000 — $190,000 USD

new_roles.description:
Job Title: Head of Operations
 Employment Status: Full-time
 Office Hours: Monday - Friday; 4:1 hybrid schedule
 Location: Boston, Massachusetts
 Compensation: $175,000-200,000 base + variable + equity options
*compensation may be negotiated based on experience level

 About Ketryx: 

 Ketryx is an AI platform that enables healthcare and life sciences companies to ship life-saving products in weeks instead of years.

 Exploding product complexity is burying companies in compliance paperwork and blocking innovation. Our AI software removes this friction, dissolving the historical tradeoff between innovation and compliance, and enables regulated industries to innovate at the pace of modern software.

 Ketryx already touches the lives of millions of patients and powers 4 of the world’s top 5 life science companies and 25% of the Fortune 500 life science market. Backed by Lightspeed Ventures, our founders are the former Head of AI at Amgen and CTO of Wolfram Cloud.

 Healthcare and life sciences is just the beginning for us. Automotive, aerospace, energy — if it’s regulated, it’s because society decided it matters. These products move humanity, shape our future, and are safety-critical. Come join us and help build the AI platform to power safe innovation.

 The Role 

 We're hiring a Head of Operations to own all things operations & people as Ketryx scales. You'll inherit a small, capable team and a company that is growing quickly across the US and Europe, with all the ambiguity and opportunity that comes with it. Your mandate is over the people here at Ketryx & how we work, by building + refining our systems, hiring engine, and culture that allow us to grow fast and execute without losing what makes our team effective.

 This is a hands-on leadership role based in Boston, including quarterly travel to our Vienna office. You'll set our strategy around cross-functional collaboration, be responsible for designing how we work, and answer a tactical People question in Slack. Our customers build products that keep people alive. The faster we help them ship safely, the sooner these products reach patients. How well we hire, develop, and support our own team is critical!

 You will report to Erez, our CEO and Co-founder

 Responsibilities 

 Business operations 

 
 Build and run the operating system. Design Ketryx's operating rhythm end to end: weekly leadership meetings, monthly business reviews, quarterly planning and retros, and annual goal setting. Make it one cadence across Boston and Vienna.

 Own planning and OKRs. Lead the annual and multi-year operating plan with Erez and Finance. Run the company-wide OKR process, from setting goals to grading them.

 Define and track company KPIs. Set the metrics that tell us whether we're winning across GTM, Product, Engineering, and Delivery. Build a single source of truth for them, and use AI tools to automate the reporting instead of assembling it by hand.

 Drive cross-functional initiatives. Take the company's highest-priority projects that span teams, resolve ownership gaps, and see them through. Lead root-cause analysis when something critical breaks.

 Build for the next stage. Spot where our processes, tools, and structures won't hold as we grow, and fix them before they break. Over time, hire and lead a small business operations team.

 
 People & talent strategy 

 
 Lead the Talent and People leaders. Manage our (Director/Manager) of Talent Acquisition and (Director/Manager) of People. They own day-to-day execution in their departments; you set direction, coach them, and hold their teams to annual goals and metrics tied to company OKRs.

 Set the people strategy. Translate the company plan into a people plan: where we invest in headcount, which capabilities we build or buy, and how the org should be structured as we scale.

 
 Required Skills 

 
 8+ years in HR/People Operations with at least three leading the function or a major pillar of it, especially at high growth startups

 Strong opinions on what can work, a willingness to try something new, and a network of People leaders to tap into for broader questions

 Direct experience scaling a company through significant headcount growth — you've seen what breaks at 100, 200, 500 people and have opinions about it

 Comfort operating without a large team or established playbook — you build the thing and then run it

 Strong recruiting instincts; you can assess engineering and GTM talent markets and partner credibly with engineering leaders

 Demonstrated ownership of compensation and leveling design

 Multi-country employment experience (US and EU) or clear evidence you can get up to speed fast

 Sound judgment in ambiguous, confidential situations, and the directness to bring hard news to the leadership team early

 
 Preferred Skills 

 
 Experience supporting distributed teams across US and European time zones

 
 What We Offer 

 
 Competitive compensation

 Generous stock options possible

 Work in an exciting field with a positive impact on the world

 Opportunity to learn and grow as part of a global team

 Generous PTO for full-time

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Regulatory Operations
new_roles.description:
Company Overview: 

 Prime Medicine is a leading biotechnology company dedicated to creating and delivering the next generation of gene editing therapies to patients. The Company is leveraging its proprietary Prime Editing platform, a versatile, precise and efficient gene editing technology, to develop a new class of differentiated, one-time, potentially curative genetic therapies. Designed to make only the right edit at the right position within a gene while minimizing unwanted DNA modifications, Prime Editors have the potential to repair almost all types of genetic mutations and work in many different tissues, organs and cell types.  

 Prime Medicine is currently progressing a diversified portfolio of investigational therapeutic programs organized around our core areas of focus: hematology, immunology & oncology, liver and lung. Across each core area, Prime Medicine is focused initially on a set of high value programs, each targeting a disease with well-understood biology and a clearly defined clinical development and regulatory path, and each expected to provide the foundation for expansion into additional opportunities. For more information, please visit www.primemedicine.com .

 Position Summary

 The Senior Manager, Regulatory Operations will plan, coordinate, and drive execution of regulatory submissions and program timelines across Prime Medicine's product pipeline. This role partners closely with Regulatory Affairs, CMC, Nonclinical, Clinical, and Quality teams to ensure submissions to global health authorities (including the FDA and EMA) are complete, high-quality, and delivered on schedule. The ideal candidate brings strong project management discipline, deep familiarity with regulatory submission processes, and the ability to keep cross-functional teams aligned under tight timelines.

 Key Responsibilities

 
 Submission Planning & Execution: Lead end-to-end planning and execution of regulatory submissions, including INDs/CTAs, BLAs/MAAs, amendments, annual reports, and briefing packages.

 Timeline & Risk Management: Develop and maintain integrated regulatory timelines, track milestones and dependencies, identify critical-path risks, and drive mitigation plans.

 Cross-Functional Coordination: Partner with Regulatory Affairs, CMC, Nonclinical, Clinical, Quality, and external partners to compile, quality-check, and finalize submission content.

 Health Authority Interactions: Support preparation for health authority meetings, including briefing books, logistics, meeting minutes, and action item tracking.

 Information Requests: Track incoming health authority information requests (IRs) and coordinate timely, well-organized responses across functional teams.

 Document & Systems Management: Manage regulatory publishing and document management systems, ensuring submissions meet eCTD and other applicable technical standards.

 Process & Compliance: Maintain regulatory operations SOPs and tracking systems; identify and implement process improvements to increase efficiency and quality.

 Vendor & Budget Oversight: Support management of regulatory operations vendors and budget, including publishing and translation vendors.

 
 Required Qualifications

 
 Bachelor's degree in life sciences, regulatory affairs, or a related field.

 7+ years of experience in regulatory affairs or regulatory operations within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.

 Demonstrated experience managing IND/CTA and BLA/MAA submissions from planning through filing.

 Strong working knowledge of eCTD structure, regulatory publishing tools, and document management systems (e.g., Veeva Vault RIM or similar).

 Proven project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent programs and competing priorities.

 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management abilities.

 High attention to detail and a strong quality mindset.

 
 Preferred Qualifications

 
 Experience supporting rare disease or orphan drug development programs.

 Experience with gene therapy, gene editing, or cell therapy regulatory submissions.

 Experience with expedited programs such as Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track, RMAT, or Orphan Drug Designation.

 PMP or other formal project management certification.

 Advanced degree (MS, PharmD, or PhD) in a scientific discipline.

 Experience working with global (ex-US) health agencies, such as the EMA, MHRA, Health Canada, Swissmedic, or PMDA.

 The pay range reflects the full-time base salary range we expect to pay for this role at the time of posting. Base pay will be determined based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, skills, and education. This role is eligible for an annual short-term incentive award (e.g., bonus) and an annual long-term incentive award (e.g., equity).

 Prime Medicine offers a comprehensive Total Rewards package with robust health, financial, and wellness benefits—including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, a 401(k) match, and equity programs—along with generous paid time off, wellness days, and company-wide recharge breaks.

 Our commitment to employee well-being reflects our belief that when we care for our people, we strengthen our ability to put patients first and make meaningful impact together.

 U.S. Pay Range
 $149,000 — $166,000 USD 


 Prime Medicine is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, or any other classification protected by law.

new_roles.description:
About Commonwealth Fusion Systems: 
 
Commonwealth Fusion Systems is on a mission to deliver the urgent transition to fusion energy.
 
Combining decades of research, top talent, and new technologies, we’re designing and building commercially viable fusion power plants. And we're working with policymakers, suppliers, and many others to build the energy industry of the future.
 
We’re in the best position to make it happen. Since 2018, we’ve raised $4 billion of capital, making us the largest and leading fusion company in the world.
 
Now we’re looking for more thinkers, doers, builders, and makers to join us. People who’ll bring new perspectives, solve tough problems, and thrive as part of a team. 
 
If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you.


Join the power movement as Senior Manager, Accounting Operations
 
Our Accounting team is looking for a transformational leader to own and optimize our operational accounting functions. This person must have a broad knowledge of accounting and experience in developing and scaling a talented team. The Senior Manager, Accounting Operations acts as a connector between our Accounting function and adjacent teams including Payroll, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, etc. We are looking for someone who is anticipatory and able to look five steps ahead in the process to see how accounting decisions affect everything part of our organization. The role is structural in nature: it creates one clear owner for work that is currently fragmented across staff, consultants, and senior accounting leadership, reducing operational bottlenecks and helping the Accounting organization scale as CFS grows.You will lead us through optimization efforts to develop and implement best practices and effective systems as we continue to scale the company, but also won't be afraid to be hands-on when necessary. This role has immense opportunity for growth as our team continues to grow and develop.

What you'll do:
Evaluate, recommend, and implement process improvements for accounting operations, including analyzing potential system enhancements and developing SOPs
Own collaboration with Supply Chain, FP&A, People Ops, IT, etc. to ensure optimized processes and cross-functional communication
Manage and develop the AP, payroll, expense reporting, and state filing compliance team and operations; build role clarity, cross-training, backup coverage, and accountability
Serve as the first-line manager-level owner for operational accounting issue triage, escalation handling, root-cause follow-up, and process discipline
Document key operating procedures, create scalable SOPs and training materials, and ensure process changes are communicated and adopted across impacted functions
Monitor operational accounting metrics and recurring issues to identify trends, reduce rework, and improve processing accuracy and cycle time
What we’re looking for:
Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration or Accounting or similar field preferred
Minimum of 7 years of relevant accounting, accounting operations, or finance operations experience
Minimum of 5 years of supervisory, team lead, or process-owner experience in a finance/accounting environment
Hands-on experience with AP, payroll coordination, expense reporting, state filing compliance, or related operational accounting workflows
Demonstrated experience improving processes, resolving operational bottlenecks, documenting procedures, and driving accountability across functions
Experience working cross-functionally with teams such as Supply Chain, FP&A, People Ops/HR, ERP/IT, operations, or procurement
Strong process ownership, issue triage, prioritization, and root-cause problem-solving skills
Ability to manage ambiguity, create structure, and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment
Strong communication skills and ability to partner with non-accounting stakeholders while maintaining compliance and control discipline
People leadership, coaching, staff development, and accountability management
Strong Excel and ERP fluency; ability to use data to identify exceptions, trends, and process gaps
Bonus points for: 
Experience in a high-growth, manufacturing, R&D, project-based, or operationally complex environment
Experience with Odoo or similar ERP systems
Experience managing external providers for state filings, compliance, payroll support, or related services
Experience with corporate card programs, travel and expense systems, procure-to-pay workflows, or payroll systems
CPA, CPP, or other relevant professional certification
Experience building SOPs, training materials, controls documentation, and audit-ready support
Must-have Requirements: 
Perform extended activities such as typing, standing, sitting, walking, etc.
Occasional nights/weekends/on-call may be required during payroll processing, month-end close, audit, compliance deadlines, system issues, or urgent operational escalations.
Work in a facility that contains industrial hazards including heat, cold, noise, fumes, strong magnets, lead (Pb), high voltage, high current, pressure systems, and cryogenics

new_roles.title: Director, Technical Services/Manufacturing Science
new_roles.description:
At Elanco (NYSE: ELAN) – it all starts with animals! 
 
 As a global leader in animal health, we are dedicated to innovation and delivering products and services to prevent and treat disease in farm animals and pets. At Elanco, we are driven by our vision of Food and Companionship Enriching Life and our purpose – all to Go Beyond for Animals, Customers, Society and Our People. 
 
 At Elanco, we pride ourselves on fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment. We believe that diversity is the driving force behind innovation, creativity, and overall business success. Here, you’ll be part of a company that values and champions new ways of thinking, work with dynamic individuals, and acquire new skills and experiences that will propel your career to new heights. 
 
 Making animals’ lives better makes life better – join our team today! 
 
 
 Your Role: Director – Technical Service/Manufacturing Science (TSMS) 
 
 As the TSMS Director, you will lead a high-performing team of scientists and engineers responsible for the technical stewardship of all manufacturing processes at the Fort Dodge site. In this role, you will drive technical strategy, ensure GMP compliance, and foster a culture of innovation to support current production and future growth.
 
 Your Responsibilities: 
 Provide strategic technical leadership for manufacturing processes including biological antigen production, aseptic processing, vaccine formulation, and filling.
 Ensure regulatory compliance and operational excellence through robust application of GMP, periodic product reviews, and process validation activities.
 Lead, coach, and develop a technical team of scientists, engineers, and statisticians to create a high-performance culture of accountability.
 Champion site safety and environmental stewardship by ensuring safe laboratory and pilot plant operations and participating in hazard assessments.
 Drive continuous process improvement and technical problem-solving by leveraging data analytics and collaborating across the Elanco network.
 
 What You Need to Succeed (minimum qualifications): 
 Education: Bachelor’s in engineering (Chemical, Mechanical, Bioprocess), Chemistry, Microbiology, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
 Experience: Minimum of 10+ years of experience in pharmaceutical, animal health, or biotechnology manufacturing with progressive leadership in technical services or process engineering.
 Top 2 skills: Deep understanding of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and proven ability to lead and develop high-performing technical teams through complex problem-solving.
 
 What will give you a competitive edge (preferred qualifications): 
 Master’s degree in related discipline
 Direct experience with vaccine manufacturing, viral or bacterial antigen production, aseptic processing, or lyophilization.
 Experience managing process validation, technology transfers, and investigations in a regulated environment.
 Demonstrated ability to interface effectively with Quality, Engineering, and Regulatory teams to influence business outcomes.
 Experience working within a matrixed, global technical organization with a strong professional network.
 Track record of mentoring and developing early-career technical talent for leadership pipelines.
 
 Additional Information: 
 Travel: 10%
 Location: Fort Dodge, IA - Site-Based
 
 Don't meet every single requirement? Studies have shown underrecognized groups are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At Elanco we are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive work environment. If you think you might be a good fit for a role but don't necessarily meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. You may be the right candidate for this role or other roles!
 
 Elanco Benefits and Perks: 
 We offer a comprehensive benefits package focusing on financial, physical, and mental well-being while encouraging our employees to pursue our purpose! Some highlights include:
 
• Multiple relocation packages
• Two weeklong shutdowns (mid-summer and year-end) in the US (in addition to PTO)
• 8-week parental leave
• 9 Employee Resource Groups
• Annual bonus offering
• Flexible work arrangements
• Up to 6% 401K matching
 
 Elanco is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status

These tools help ensure a consistent, structured evaluation, but they do not make hiring decisions. All decisions involve a human reviewer. new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality (Floor Leader)
new_roles.description:
At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.”  As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way.  We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together.  

 The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities:  we come together ,  we always look for a better way , and  we create possibilities . 

 Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must be able to maintain such authorization without current or future employer or school sponsorship. GE Appliances will not sponsor employment-based visas for this position now or in the future.

 Interested in joining us on our journey? 

he Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for plant quality performance, compliance, and continuous improvement within a high-volume manufacturing environment. This role leads the Quality Floor team and oversees production quality, component testing, Manufacturing Control Plan (MCP) auditing, and quality improvement initiatives to ensure products and processes consistently meet established standards.

Partnering closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supplier Quality, and other cross-functional teams, this leader drives structured problem-solving, root cause analysis, and corrective and preventive actions to reduce defects, minimize scrap and rework, and improve process capability. The Senior Manager establishes a proactive quality culture by strengthening process controls, reinforcing standard work, and using data-driven insights to identify risks and prevent recurring issues. Through strong team leadership and a focus on sustainable results, this role helps improve product reliability, reduce the cost of poor quality, and strengthen manufacturing performance. 
 Position 
Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality (Floor Leader) 
 Location 
USA, Decatur, AL 
 
 How You'll Create Possibilities 
 Live, promote and support the Appliance Production System (APS) philosophy and drive continuous improvement in the quality and adjacent areas.  Coach all team members to ensure cross-functional, focused collaboration is the way we work. 
 Partner with the Product Line Quality, Business Operations and Manufacturing Engineering Leaders to promote a culture that establishes, sustains and improves product quality through engineering problem solving and discipline around supporting systems.  Promote a method-based quick response to new issues. 
 Responsible for developing team performance metrics tied to the overall factory (FPY, EOLA, Scrap) and product line financial plan (Warranty, Damage, Concessions, Scrap, Consumer Education).  Leads team to identify and complete projects and tasks supporting this effort.  Owns and assigns tasks and establishes accountability at the appropriate level.    
 Closely collaborates with the product line Engineering, Field Quality and Service organizations to understand and respond to part or system product level performance issues impacting owner use and satisfaction. Responds to this data in addition to internal data streams (leading indicators) for product quality and reliability (Engineering, EOLA and CAT / CUT labs).   
 Identify and execute projects to improve the costing of operations, broad owner for Corrective and Preventative Actions (CAPA), Corrective Action Request (CAR) approach to problem solving. 
 Work with Design, Operations and Quality Leadership to prioritize funding/resources to meet targets, support Continuous Improvement. 
 Owner of all attributes of the Manufacturing Control Plan for broad areas.  Responsible for the training, execution, auditing and improvement of the Manufacturing Quality Control Plan.  Support efforts intended to improve work station documentation process; create, update and maintain Manufacturing Control Instructions (MCI’s), visual aid and alerts (single point lessons) as needed. 
 Provide technical oversight to drive the development, sustainment and continuous improvement of factory quality. 
 
 
 What You'll Bring to Our Team 
 Bachelor of Science Degree in Engineering or related discipline
 7+ years of experience with manufacturing quality/NPI quality projects and process improvement
 Experience with product and process Quality Management System development and implementation
 Previous team and project leadership, including demonstration of goal setting, monitoring of performance v goals and a strong feedback / development / accountability cycle 
 Must be skilled in Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Minitab and Outlook.
 
 Working Conditions: 
 Working conditions are normal for a high-volume manufacturing environment.
 Working in this environment requires the use of safety equipment to include but not limited to; eye safety glasses, hearing protectors, work boots, and hard hats.
 These roles require frequent walking in a manufacturing plant environment.
 Hours & Weekends: Working off-shift and weekends may be required.
 
 
 Our Culture 
 Our work is centered on our People and Culture as reflected in our Zero Distance philosophy and we recognize the importance of reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and diversity (I&D). This underscores our commitment to fostering an environment where every individual feels valued, connected, and empowered to contribute, while positioning our organization to adapt seamlessly to the evolving needs of our workforce and communities. 

 This reflects our dedication to creating solutions that: Empower colleagues by fostering an environment where all voices are heard, valued, and encouraged to contribute. Strengthen communities where we live and work. Reinforce a culture of belonging, purpose, and engagement. Reflect the diversity of the communities we serve through our workforce, products, and practices. 

 By further embedding Zero Distance into our People and Culture framework, we will continue to build a deeply connected organization. We are cultivating a culture of engagement, belonging, and connection, because while attracting new talent remains a priority, retention is a cornerstone of our strategy. 
 
 
 
 GE Appliances is a trust-based organization. It is important we offer our employees the flexibility they need to do their best work while balancing the needs of the business and individuals. When you join GE Appliances, you will have the opportunity to work with your leader to create a flexible work arrangement that balances the needs of the individual, team, and organization. 
 
 
 GE Appliances is an Equal Opportunity Employer.  Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. 
 
 GE Appliances participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S 
 
 
 If you are an individual with a disability and need assistance or an accommodation to use our website or to apply, please send an e-mail to ask.recruiting@geappliances.com

identity_held_roles.title: Head of Aircraft Quality (R6146)
identity_held_roles.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


About Shield AI:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense technology company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Our products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. 
Job Description:
We’re looking for a hands-on quality leader to take X-BAT from early prototype builds through production launch and into rate production. 
You will build the aircraft quality organization and establish the quality capability for our new Seattle-area production facility, X-Forge 3. You’ll own product and process quality across prototype, pre-series and production builds, ensuring that lessons from development become effective controls as the program scales. 
This role owns the Quality Management System, quality engineering, inspection, nonconformance management and audit readiness for the X-BAT manufacturing operation. You’ll partner with Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Production and Supply Chain to prevent defects, resolve recurring problems and deliver aircraft that meet technical, customer and applicable regulatory requirements. 
We need a technically credible leader who can build practical, scalable systems, make sound decisions under schedule pressure and challenge senior stakeholders constructively while keeping execution moving. 

What you'll do:
Build quality into prototype and launch
Lead quality planning and execution for X-BAT prototype and development builds, establishing appropriate inspection, test evidence and build records as designs evolve.
Partner with Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering to identify product and process risks, define critical controls and build quality requirements into tooling, work instructions and test plans.
Establish configuration and traceability controls with Engineering and Production, ensuring each aircraft’s build status, deviations and nonconformances are understood and documented.
Capture lessons from build, integration and test issues, and drive their incorporation into design changes, manufacturing processes and future builds.
Define quality readiness criteria for pre-series builds and production launch, validating inspection methods, process controls, workforce competence and closure of significant risks.
Establish the Seattle quality operation
Recruit, develop and lead the quality team, building the technical capability and frontline support needed as aircraft production grows.
Establish and maintain a lean, effective QMS for X-Forge 3, aligned with Shield AI’s wider quality framework, AS9100, ISO 9001 and applicable customer requirements.
Lead certification readiness and internal, customer and external audits, driving timely closure and sustained effectiveness of corrective actions.
Set up receiving, in-process and final inspection capability, including measurement equipment, calibration, training and quality records, in partnership with relevant functions.
Deliver quality at rate
Own production quality performance, using first-pass yield, defects, rework and escapes to focus action where it improves aircraft quality and production flow.
Lead containment, root cause analysis and corrective action for manufacturing quality issues, with clear functional ownership and verification that fixes prevent recurrence.
Own the nonconformance and MRB process, ensuring disposition decisions follow approved technical authority and that affected hardware remains controlled.
Partner with Supply Chain and supplier quality teams to resolve incoming quality issues and improve supplier performance before defects disrupt aircraft builds.
Work with Engineering and Production to define acceptance evidence and ensure aircraft meet approved requirements before release.
Use digital quality tools and manufacturing data to strengthen traceability, expose trends and reduce manual administration as production scales.
Give leadership a clear view of quality performance, product risks and readiness; escalate or stop affected work when requirements or product integrity cannot be assured.
Required qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality or a related technical field.
10+ years of leadership experience in quality, product assurance or reliability within aerospace, defense technology or high-reliability manufacturing.
Demonstrated success leading quality through prototype or new product introduction and into sustained production.
Proven ability to build and scale quality teams and systems while supporting fast-paced development and manufacturing operations.
Deep expertise in containment, root cause analysis, MRB, corrective and preventive action, and continuous improvement.
Strong working knowledge of AS9100 and ISO 9001, with practical implementation and audit leadership experience.
Experience with complex assembly, inspection, configuration control, traceability and product acceptance.
Ability to influence and challenge senior leaders constructively across Engineering, Production and Supply Chain.
A hands-on leadership style and sound technical judgment, balancing timely execution with clear quality standards and accountability.
Preferred qualifications:
Direct experience taking a new aircraft program from prototype through production launch and rate ramp.
Experience establishing quality capability at a new manufacturing facility or transferring production between sites.
Experience in aircraft final assembly, systems integration, production test and reliability improvement.
Experience deploying digital quality systems, statistical process controls and data-driven defect prevention.
Advanced degree in engineering, quality or a related technical discipline.

Job Description:
Shield AI is seeking a highly driven Sr. Manager Materials Planning & Logistics to lead supply planning, material readiness, production planning, and logistics execution for next-generation autonomous aircraft development programs and a new greenfield manufacturing facility. This leadership role is accountable for establishing the people, processes, systems, and infrastructure required to support rapid product development, new product introduction, and the transition to scalable rate production. 
The ideal candidate combines strong operational leadership with hands-on execution, thrives in fast-paced environments, and has experience building manufacturing and supply chain capabilities from the ground up. You will work cross-functionally with Engineering, Program Management, Quality, Procurement, and Operations teams.  

What you'll do:
Development Program Materials Planning  
Own the materials planning, production control, inventory, warehousing, and logistics strategy.
Partner with Engineering, Program Management, and Procurement to develop and maintain accurate build plans that are aligned with program milestones.  
Define and monitor key performance indicators for schedule attainment, material availability, shortage reduction, inventory health, work-order execution, and planning accuracy.
Identify long-lead material risks and implement mitigation strategies to protect schedule.
Oversee the development and execution of material recovery plans.
Drive engineering change management processes to support rapid development and ECO implementation.  
Develop planning models that support rapid prototyping, design iteration, and low-rate initial production activities.  
Support executive-level program and operations reviews by clearly communicating material status, risks, business impacts, and required decisions.
Greenfield Facility Build & Operational Readiness  
Lead planning and logistics readiness activities for a new manufacturing facility.  
Design and implement warehouse, stockroom, and material flow processes from receiving through point-of-use consumption.  
Establish inventory control procedures, material storage standards, and transaction discipline.  
Partner with Manufacturing Engineering and Facilities teams to optimize material movement and operational efficiency.  
Team Leadership  
Create a culture focused on accountability, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and mission execution.  
Establish standard work and training programs.  
Drive cross-functional collaboration to solve complex challenges.
Required qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or related field.  
7+ years of experience in materials planning, inventory management, or supply chain operations.  
Experience supporting complex hardware development programs in aerospace, defense, automotive, robotics, or advanced manufacturing environments.  
Demonstrated experience implementing or scaling material planning and inventory management processes.  
Strong understanding of MRP/ERP systems and supply chain planning methodologies.  
Experience managing material readiness for new product introduction (NPI) and engineering development programs.  
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, highly dynamic environment with evolving priorities.  
Excellent analytical, organizational, and communication skills.  
U.S. citizenship and ability to obtain/maintain a security clearance
Preferred qualifications:
Experience supporting greenfield manufacturing facility launches or major facility expansions.  
Aerospace, defense, unmanned systems, or advanced technology manufacturing experience.  
Experience with Oracle, SAP, Costpoint, or similar ERP platforms.  
APICS/ASCM certifications (CPIM, CSCP) or equivalent.  
Familiarity with ITAR, EAR, DFARS, and government contracting requirements.  
Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or operational excellence experience.  
Experience supporting production ramp and transition from development to rate manufacturing.
Why Shield AI:
At Shield AI, you'll help build technology that matters. You'll work alongside world-class engineers, operators, and innovators solving some of the most challenging problems in autonomy and national security. This is a unique opportunity to shape the foundation of a rapidly growing aerospace and defense company while helping bring revolutionary autonomous systems into operational service.

identity_held_roles.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


Job Description:
The Senior Manager of Quality is responsible for establishing and leading all quality activities for a complex aerospace development program from prototype through production readiness. This role serves as the primary quality leader embedded within the program team and partners closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Flight Test, and Program Management to ensure products are designed, developed, tested, and transitioned to production with quality, reliability, and mission success as foundational objectives.
The Senior Manager of Quality will build and lead a multidisciplinary quality team while implementing scalable quality systems, risk management processes, problem-solving disciplines, and development quality practices appropriate for a rapidly growing aerospace and defense technology organization.
This position requires balancing speed of development with disciplined engineering rigor to support aggressive program schedules while ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and company requirements.

What you'll do:
Development Quality Leadership
Serve as the quality leader for XBAT development.
Establish quality strategy, objectives, and metrics aligned with program milestones.
Integrate quality requirements into the product development lifecycle.
Ensure quality considerations are incorporated during system architecture, design reviews, verification, validation, and qualification activities.
Partner with Engineering leadership to identify and mitigate technical and programmatic risks.
Drive a culture of proactive quality and continuous improvement throughout the program.
Design & Configuration Quality
Ensure quality requirements are appropriately captured in product definitions, specifications, and design documentation.
Participate in design reviews, change control boards, and configuration management activities.
Ensure full configuration and traceability for all material installed into prototype aircraft.
Evaluate engineering changes for quality and production readiness impacts.
Support requirements verification and validation planning.
Drive design-for-manufacturing, design-for-quality, and design-for-reliability initiatives.
Risk Management & Reliability
Lead quality participation in program risk management activities.
Establish and maintain FRACAS processes for development and flight test phases of the program.
Facilitate root cause and corrective action investigations for design, manufacturing, supplier, and field failures.
Support reliability growth planning and execution.
Monitor defect trends, failure modes, and reliability metrics to identify systemic risks.
Verification, Validation & Test Quality
Develop quality oversight strategies for laboratory, ground, and flight test activities.
Ensure test results, anomalies, and nonconformances are appropriately documented and dispositioned.
Support qualification and certification efforts.
Establish processes for managing test escapes, failures, and corrective actions.
Nonconformance & Corrective Action Management
Lead Material Review Board activities for development hardware.
Establish scalable processes for nonconformance management.
Drive root cause analysis using structured problem-solving methodologies.
Ensure timely and effective corrective and preventive actions.
Track effectiveness of corrective actions through closure.
Production Readiness & Industrialization
Partner with Manufacturing and Supply Chain teams to transition products from prototype to production.
Define quality requirements for production readiness reviews.
Support development of inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and control strategies.
Ensure lessons learned from development are incorporated into production processes.
Lead quality planning activities supporting low-rate initial production and rate increases.
Quality Management System
Develop and implement quality processes supporting aerospace development programs.
Ensure compliance with AS9100, customer requirements, and internal procedures.
Drive continuous improvement of development quality processes.
Support internal and external audits as required.
Establish scalable systems that support future production growth.
Leadership & Team Development
Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing quality organization.
Recruit and develop quality engineers, inspectors, and technicians.
Establish clear objectives, priorities, and performance expectations.
Promote a culture of accountability, technical excellence, and collaboration.
Develop organizational capabilities to support future company growth.
Required qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Aerospace Engineering, or related technical discipline.
10+ years of experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, space, or other highly regulated industries.
5+ years of leadership experience managing technical quality organizations.
Experience supporting complex product development programs from concept through production transition.
Strong knowledge of quality systems, engineering development processes, and aerospace manufacturing.
Experience leading root cause investigations and corrective action programs.
Experience with risk management, reliability engineering, and failure analysis.
Working knowledge of AS9100 quality management systems.
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior leadership.
Preferred qualifications:
Experience supporting UAV, aerospace, defense, aviation, autonomous systems, or advanced technology programs.
Experience leading quality organizations during rapid company growth.
Background in systems engineering, reliability engineering, or development engineering.
Experience with flight test programs and qualification testing.
ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), or equivalent certification.
Familiarity with government defense programs and customer quality requirements.

identity_held_roles.description:

Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. What you'll do:
Develop the supplier quality team responsible for supplier qualification, surveillance, performance management, and corrective-action activities across Shield AI’s global aerospace and defense supply base.
Establish supplier-quality priorities, allocate resources, and translate functional objectives into staffing, workload, and execution plans that support product, program, and organizational needs.
Develop Supplier Quality leaders and engineering personnel through coaching, performance management, succession planning, workforce development, and technical mentorship.
Oversee supplier qualification, risk assessments, periodic performance reviews, supplier audits, source inspections, and approved-supplier status across complex aerospace hardware, commodities, and manufacturing processes.
Ensure supplier requirements are effectively flowed down and that suppliers comply with applicable quality management system, engineering, customer, contractual, regulatory, and statutory requirements.
Escalate significant supplier-quality risks and direct SCARs, supplier recovery efforts, and capability-improvement plans that could affect product quality, delivery, mission readiness, or program execution.
Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, and Program teams to address supplier producibility, design-for-manufacturability, process capability, technical execution, and quality risks.
Advance supplier-quality processes, business systems, data analytics, and continuous-improvement practices that strengthen supplier capability, product quality, delivery performance, and supply-base resilience.
Required qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or another related technical discipline.
At least 7 years of relevant experience, including 2–5 years of leadership or people-management experience with direct responsibility for Quality Engineering and/or Supplier Quality Engineering personnel.
Strong working knowledge of AS9100 and/or ISO 9001 quality-management systems, as well as aerospace and defense supplier-quality requirements.
Demonstrated proficiency in root-cause analysis and structured problem-solving methods, including 8D, 5 Whys, and fishbone analysis.
Experience with supplier qualification, supplier development, PPAP, and First Article Inspection processes, including AS9102 requirements.
Understanding of ITAR, EAR, DFARS, and other requirements applicable to aerospace and defense suppliers.
Demonstrated people-leadership capability, including coaching, performance management, organizational development, and building high-performing technical teams.
Strong cross-functional collaboration, executive communication, and supplier relationship-management skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook.
Experience using ERP/MRP systems.
Ability to travel to Shield AI manufacturing locations and supplier sites domestically and, as needed, internationally—up to approximately 20% of the time.

ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Quality Manager (CQM), or equivalent quality certification.
Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.
Experience leading supplier-quality functions in a high-growth aerospace, defense, autonomy, robotics, or advanced-manufacturing environment.
Experience supporting the production and qualification of complex electromechanical, electronic, precision-machined, composite, or avionics hardware.

identity_held_roles.description:
Application close date:
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed. 
 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!    
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities. 
 
 We are seeking a dynamic Senior Manager of Manufacturing Engineering and Technology to oversee our aerospace component production processes. This pivotal role will lead teams in achieving operational excellence while collaborating with cross-functional departments to continuously enhance manufacturing operations. The ideal candidate will be results-driven, adept at resource management, and committed to maintaining high-quality standards in a fast-paced environment.
 
 We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!
 
 Position Specific Details: 
 Location: Space Coast, FL
 Relocation: Available
 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Lead and optimize manufacturing operations to ensure efficiency and quality.
 Develop and execute production plans to meet delivery schedules.
 Mentor manufacturing teams, providing guidance and fostering a positive work environment, encouraging teamwork and openness, and sharing information to foster unity.
 Collaborate with engineering, quality, and supply chain teams to address manufacturing challenges, balancing day-to-day activities with strategic planning.
 Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance production processes and metrics.
 Monitor production performance and provide regular updates to senior management, demonstrating sound judgment and understanding the impact of team actions on business drivers and adapting to industry changes.
 Ensure compliance with safety, regulatory, and company standards, and take initiative on opportunities and challenges with urgency and enthusiasm.
 Manage budget and resource allocation for manufacturing activities.
 Support new product introductions and scale up production capabilities.
 Evaluate inputs and criteria to make informed decisions with a focus on decision quality.
 
 Team Focus & Domain Expertise: 
 In this role you will lead and mentor a team of Manufacturing Engineers and Planners who are developing and supporting the design and fabrication of machined parts, advanced metal forming, and wire harnesses. identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality
identity_held_roles.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.




THE ROLE:

The Senior Manager, Quality owns program quality end to end and leads the Quality Engineering team that supports it. You will build and lead a team of Quality Engineers across the program's process areas, owning requirements into our AS9100D quality management system, and be the single point of accountability for whether product is built to spec, on schedule, and with the objective quality evidence to prove it.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Team leadership — build, lead, and develop the Quality Engineering team supporting the project across sheet metal, welding and forming, NDT, foundry and forging, machining, and additive manufacturing.

• Staffing and coverage — close the open QE positions on the program, set priorities, and ensure every process area has quality coverage.

• Development and standards — coach QEs, set consistent standards of practice, and grow special-process competency (welding, NDT) across the team.

• Cross-functional partnership — represent quality with Build Engineering, Operations, and the program team, and serve as the escalation point for quality decisions on Nautilus.

• Program quality for Nautilus — first-article inspection (AS9102), product qualification, and quality across the build from receipt to delivery.

• Non-conformance and corrective action — control non-conforming material and customer escapes, drive root-cause and corrective action to closure, and own escape management for the program.

• Supplier and receiving quality — flow requirements to suppliers, verify certifications and OQE at receipt, and build receiving capability for controlled material.

• Audit readiness — prepare for and lead customer, and AS9100 audits for the program, and own the internal-audit posture that keeps it compliant.

• Metrics and reporting — quality KPIs, escape trends, and program quality status to leadership.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

• 8+ years in quality within defense, marine, nuclear, or aerospace manufacturing, including direct people-management of a quality team.

• Proven command of AS9100 / ISO 9001 and hands-on experience integrating customer and regulatory requirements into a QMS.

• Track record building quality processes and teams in a fast-scaling or startup manufacturing environment.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance; U.S. person under ITAR.



What Will Set You Apart

• Background at a submarine prime or shipyard (e.g., General Dynamics Electric Boat, HII Newport News) or a qualified SUBSAFE supplier.

• Knowledge of NAVSEA and SUBSAFE / Material Level I requirements (objective quality evidence, controlled material, traceability, cleanliness).

• AS9100 / ISO 9001 lead-auditor certification; familiarity with welding and NDT special-process controls (Nadcap).

• CQE, CMQ/OE, or equivalent quality certification.

• Experience standing up program quality from the ground up — writing the system, not just running it.




BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
 401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy https://www.hadrian.co/privacy-policy.

 


CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 


HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

Commissioning Chief Engineer, Marauder

Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing defense autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

Job Summary:

In this role you will be responsible for the commissioning and operation of the engine room and all associated machinery aboard a novel autonomous vessel. You will ensure that all marine systems — including but not limited to main propulsion, auxiliary machinery, fuel oil, lubrication, cooling, and associated environmental equipment — are properly tested and validated through structured commissioning processes and integrated with the vessel's autonomy and software control systems to support reliable manned, remote, and autonomous operation.

The ideal candidate will possess strong problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities, along with the ability to develop procedures and processes in support of a novel commissioning environment. Have a strong grasp on vessel engineering systems with the ability to work independently on issues, including drafting and refining operational and technical documentation where none previously existed. A steadfast commitment to safety and adherence to maritime regulations is essential for ensuring the highest standards in vessel operations.

Responsibilities

 - Lead and support commissioning activities for autonomous vessels, including system testing, validation, and troubleshooting prior to and during operation.

 - Collaborate with autonomy and software engineering teams to verify integration between traditional machinery control systems and the vessel's autonomy stack across manned, remote, and autonomous operating modes

 - Develop, write, and refine standard operating procedures, checklists, and technical documentation from scratch in the absence of established processes

 - Complete all necessary maintenance on vessel machinery.

 - Always be on-call while on-hitch to address any issues that arise.

 - Manage inventory and ordering of spare parts.

 - Assist in the shipboard execution of mission objectives.

 - Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously.

 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with team members, stakeholders, and senior management.

 - Problem-solving abilities and a proactive approach to addressing challenges.

 - Strong leadership skills to lead a team in a dynamic environment and pitch in when your skills are applicable while working across teams.

 - Travel to multiple locations while on hitch

Required Qualifications

 - Valid U.S. Coast Guard MMC

 - National Chief Engineer of Motor, Unlimited Horsepower Endorsement.

 - STCW Endorsements of Chief Engineer, OICEW, Basic Training, Advanced Firefighting

 - Valid USCG STCW Medical Certificate

 - Valid TWIC, USCG STCW Medical Certificate, and Passport.

 - Proficiency in maritime engineering systems, particularly electrical systems

 - Ability to work both independently and as a part of a group

 - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams

 - Pass background check and USCG/DOT drug testing prior to onboarding.

 - Security clearance and eligibility required

 - Projected 28/28 schedule

Desired Qualifications

 - Familiar with jet-drive marine engines

 - Experience with autonomous or unmanned systems

 - Experience with software engineering

 - Experience with automation systems.

Physical Demands

 - Ability to certify as “fit for work” by demonstrating ability to swim and tread water

 - Frequently and repetitively, lift, push and carry up to 50 lbs.

 - Will be exposed to marine environments, including sun, wind, rain, cold, and saltwater spray, often for extended periods

 - Must be able to operate in daylight, low-light, and night conditions using marine navigation systems and visual cues

 - Ability to perform physically demanding work i.e. stoop, lay, bend, reach, squat, kneel, crouch, twist and crawl for extended periods of time including up to 12 hours/day

 - Climb and maintain balance on ladders, platforms, or other high structures

 - Ability to stand and walk for up to 10 hours a day, including over varied and uneven terrain

 - Climb and maintain balance on ladders, scaffolding or other high structures

 - Ability to work in a hot and humid environment and follow safe practices to stay hydrated

 - Hearing ability sufficient to detect alarms, verbal instructions, and workplace hazards in a high-noise environment.

 - Must be able to work in a shipyard environment, including indoor fabrication shops, onboard vessels under construction, and outdoor areas exposed to changing weather conditions.

 - Wear Personal Protective Equipment, including but not limited to: safety glasses, safety shoes, hard hat and adhering to prescribed safety rules and guidelines

Benefits

 - Medical Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Dental and Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care

 - Saronic pays 99% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Time Off: Generous PTO and Holidays

 - Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents

 - Competitive Salary: Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

 - Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan

 - Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

 - Life and Disability Insurance: Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

 - Additional Perks: Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office

identity_held_roles.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




POSITION OVERVIEW

The Staff Quality Engineer serves as the VP of Quality's senior technical quality expert responsible for driving multi-site RCCA culture, supporting engineering and manufacturing quality. Reporting directly to the VP of Quality, this role leads enterprise-wide technical investigations, drives engineering-based Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA), and partners across Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Product, and Mission Operations to improve product reliability and operational performance.

This position applies deep engineering expertise to identify fundamental technical failure mechanisms, validate corrective actions through engineering analysis and testing, and eliminate systemic product and process risks.

The Staff Quality Engineer operates across multiple manufacturing sites and product lines, working with cross functional teams on design opportunities, manufacturing processes, and operational readiness while establishing best practices for technical problem solving across the enterprise.




TECHNICAL PROBLEM SOLVING

 - Apply structured engineering methodologies to determine true physical, process, software, or systems root causes—not simply procedural gaps.

 - Utilize advanced analytical tools including Fault Tree Analysis, Fishbone, 5 Why, Statistical Analysis, Tolerance Stack Analysis, and FMEA.

 - Validate corrective actions using engineering data, experimentation, testing, and verification.

 - Drive permanent corrective actions that eliminate recurrence across products and manufacturing sites.




MULTI-SITE QUALITY LEADERSHIP

 - Provide technical quality leadership across multiple manufacturing locations.

 - Standardize RCCA methodologies and engineering investigations across the enterprise.

 - Coach site Quality Engineers on advanced engineering problem solving.

 - Lead enterprise technical reviews for recurring issues and customer escapes.

 - Support rapid problem escalation and recovery during production interruptions.




ROOT CAUSE & CORRECTIVE ACTION (RCCA)

 - Lead enterprise RCCA for manufacturing defects, supplier escapes, customer returns, field failures, and reliability issues.

 - Ensure investigations identify technical root causes rather than symptoms.




MANUFACTURING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT

 - Improve manufacturing capability through engineering analysis.

 - Reduce defects through process optimization rather than increased inspection.

 - Support New Product Introduction (NPI) Quality activities across multiple product lines.




CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

 - Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Program Management, Product Management, Mission Operations, and Executive Leadership.

 - Present technical findings and recommendations to cross functional teams.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical or aerospace engineering.

 - 10+ years of engineering aerospace, defense, automotive, or advanced manufacturing.

 - Demonstrated success solving complex engineering problems.

 - Extensive experience leading engineering-based RCCA.

 - Experience supporting multi-site manufacturing operations.

 - Excellent communication and executive presentation skills.

 - Must be able to travel 30-50% of the time.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Design and development engineering management experience




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Establish an enterprise technical RCCA methodology across all manufacturing sites.

 - Reduce quality escapes through permanent corrective actions.

 - Improve manufacturing FPY.

 - Mentor Quality Engineers in advanced engineering problem solving.




BENEFITS

 - Medical Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Dental and Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium under the basic plan for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Time Off: Generous PTO and Holidays

 - Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents

 - Competitive Salary: Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

 - Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan with company match

 - Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

 - Life and Disability Insurance: Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

 - Pet Insurance: Discounted pet insurance options including 24/7 Telehealth helpline

 - Additional Perks: Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office
